newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start higher, Rhone jumps.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start higher, Rhone jumps.

text.p: French shares opened higher on Monday lifted by a firmer dollar on the first day of the February account while Rhone-Poulenc jumped after its unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer reported a 25 percent rise in 1996 results.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 18.83 points or 0.77 percent at 2,449.17 at 0909 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,447 from 2,429 on Friday's close.
Rhone-Poulenc up 3.97 percent at 183.30, Rorer up 3.41 percent at 436.90 francs. Rhone-Poulenc will publish its 1996 results on Thursday.
"The results were at the top end of expectations," said a dealer.
Renault, up more than five percent at 121 francs, confirmed it was seeking British part suppliers to cut costs but declined to speculate when a decision could be taken.
Renault buys some 60 billion francs in parts each year and 75 percent of that comes from French suppliers.
"This means that they are serious about looking for cost cuts and that's good news," a broker said.
Michelin was up 2.09 percent at 313 francs after Merrill Lynch changed recommendation to "buy" from "accumulate".
